subject: SignalMesh LangChain plugin + trace shim partnership inquiry
messages:
From: Elliot Barnes <elliot.barnes@signalmesh.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: SignalMesh Solutions <support@signalmesh.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Mar 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Partnership inquiry: LangChain plugin & trace shim for Redwood

Hi Markus,

Quick intro — I lead partnerships at SignalMesh. We build a lightweight request router and observability middleware for LLMs. Several of our ISV customers (LangChain authors and a couple of prompt-tooling vendors) have asked for a tightly integrated Redwood/SignalMesh experience: a LangChain plugin that can call Redwood endpoints with optimized routing, plus a trace shim that injects distributed telemetry (span IDs, model variant metadata, token-level timings) back into Redwood’s Console.

We think the combo would help customers get predictable latency + unified traces for RM/KS caching and routing decisions. Proposed pilot: 3-week technical integration with a small sample app (LangChain agent using Redwood hosted API) and a joint acceptance test that validates tracing continuity and a <15% latency overhead for the shim.

Are you the right contact for an ISV integration pilot? If so, we can send a short SOW and our security questionnaire. Happy to demo this week.

Best,
Elliot Barnes
Head of Partnerships, SignalMesh
elliot.barnes@signalmesh.com
Attachment: signalmesh-overview-1pager.pdf (application/pdf)
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Barnes <elliot.barnes@signalmesh.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 6 Mar 2025 12:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partnership inquiry: LangChain plugin & trace shim for Redwood

Hi Elliot — thanks for the note and the clear ask. I’m Markus (partnerships at Redwood). This sounds promising and aligned to our ISV integrations roadmap (LangChain/LLamaIndex ecosystem + observability plugins).

A few practical items to move things quickly:
- Please send a short SOW and your security questionnaire (SOC2 evidence, data handling, and telemetry retention).
- Proposed acceptance criteria for the 3-week pilot: (1) end-to-end trace continuity from the LangChain agent through SignalMesh into Redwood Console; (2) no more than 15% median P95 token latency increase for a standard 512-token prompt distribution; (3) a trace-level cost/attribution sample that maps to route/variant decisions.
- We’ll need a mutual action plan (owner + dates) and a contact in your eng org.

I’ve looped in Kimberly (security/compliance intake) and Marissa (ISV onboarding and SDK integration). Kimberly — can you flag any immediate blocker from compliance? Marissa — can we scope an early dev plan (SDK hooks + example LangChain plugin)?

If you can share the SOW and questionnaire today we’ll triage and get an internal kickoff set for Monday.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Head, Partnerships & Alliances | Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Elliot Barnes <elliot.barnes@signalmesh.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 7 Mar 2025 10:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partnership inquiry: LangChain plugin & trace shim for Redwood

Elliot / Markus — quick follow from compliance.

Thanks for the intro. A couple technical items we’ll need to evaluate the shim securely:
- Inventory of telemetry fields SignalMesh will forward into Redwood traces (PII-free, model metadata only).
- Retention controls and ability to opt-out of token-level persistence for specific customers.
- Signed data processing addendum (DPA) + SOC2 attachments.

On the integration side (Marissa can advise on dev specifics): we’d prefer the plugin expose a small set of hooks: pre-request routing decision (to capture chosen model/variant), post-response token timing snapshot, and an async flush path for KV cache delta. If you can provide a small reference repo (npm/pip) with example LangChain bindings that’s ideal.

Marissa — can you draft an initial dev checklist and acceptance test cases? I’ll review security artifacts once they arrive.

Kimberly
Senior Security Program Manager | Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
From: Elliot Barnes <elliot.barnes@signalmesh.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: SignalMesh Solutions <support@signalmesh.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 8 Mar 2025 11:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Partnership inquiry: LangChain plugin & trace shim for Redwood

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround. Per request, attaching two artifacts: SignalMesh_SOW_v1.pdf (pilot scope + mutual action plan) and SignalMesh_Security_Q_A.xlsx (telemetry inventory and SOC2 notes).

Highlights from the SOW:
- 3-week pilot (2 engineers from SignalMesh, 2 from Redwood)
- Deliverables: LangChain plugin demo, trace shim with example traces in Redwood Console, performance report vs. baseline, and a short joint integration doc.
- Acceptance: end-to-end trace + latency overhead under 15% P95 on our standard load harness.

We’ve also provisioned a tiny example repo: https://github.com/signalmesh/redwood-langchain-plugin (branch: pilot-prototype). It contains a minimal LangChain binding, a shim that populates trace metadata, and a short runbook for the pilot.

Next steps proposed:
1) Your team reviews SOW and questionnaire (Kimberly flagged DPA + retention controls).
2) Kickoff call Monday (Mar 10) — nominate 2 engineers each, share calendar slots.
3) We’ll open a GitHub draft PR for instrumentation points so Marissa can iterate on the sample plugin.

Let me know if that works and I’ll send a DocuSign for the SOW.

Best,
Elliot
Attachment stubs: SignalMesh_SOW_v1.pdf (application/pdf), SignalMesh_Security_Q_A.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)
